Indian indentured migration begins to British Guiana.
Indian indentured migration to Trinidad begins; NATT's General Registers begin in this year.
Direct Indian indentured migration to Suriname begins; the Lalla Rookh arrives at Paramaribo on 5 June.
The Suriname contract-labour research index covers migration through 1916.
The Trinidad General Registers end; NATT identifies the Ganges as the last ship in the series.
NATT states that the indentureship system in Trinidad was eventually abolished in 1920.
The Records of Indian Indentured Labourers are inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World framework.
